# How to Track AI Visibility in ChatGPT, Gemini & More


By OpenTools Team


Learn how to track AI visibility step by step: pick the right prompts, measure mentions, citations and sentiment, and see why Promptwatch is the best tool.


**How to Track Your AI Visibility: A Practical Step‑by‑Step Guide**


Type "best accounting software for freelancers" into ChatGPT and you won't get ten blue links. You'll get a short answer that names three or four brands, explains why each one fits, and maybe links to a couple of sources. If your brand isn't in that answer, the buyer never sees you. That's what AI visibility is about: how often, and how favorably, your brand shows up in answers from ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews. It matters more every month because a growing share of buyers now ask an AI assistant before they ever open a search engine. They ask for recommendations, comparisons and shortlists, and they often trust the answer enough to act on it. Promptwatch,[the best LLM visibility tool](https://promptwatch.com/blog/llm-visibility-tools) , will do most of the heavy lifting for you, but you still need to know what to measure and how to set things up so the numbers mean something.This guide walks you through the whole process: why spot checks fail, which metrics deserve your attention, and a step‑by‑step plan for building a tracking setup you can rely on.


**Why Manual Checks Don't Work**


Most teams start the same way. Someone opens ChatGPT, types in a few questions about their category, and takes a screenshot. If the brand shows up, everyone relaxes. If it doesn't, there's a small panic.


The problem is that the screenshot tells you almost nothing.


AI answers aren't fixed. Run the same prompt twice and you may get two different lists of brands. The model might mention you in the morning and skip you in the afternoon. That's how these systems are built. They generate a fresh answer each time, and small changes in wording or context can shift the result.


It gets messier from there. Answers also change based on:


- **Country.** A buyer in Germany may see different recommendations than a buyer in the US, even for the same question.
- **Language.** The Spanish version of a prompt can pull from entirely different sources than the English one.
- **The user.** Chat history, memory features and personal settings all shape what each person sees.
- **The platform.** Perplexity, Gemini and Claude each have their own way of finding and ranking sources, so being strong on one says little about the others.


A single person checking a handful of prompts by hand can't account for any of this. You'd need hundreds of runs, across several markets and platforms, repeated every day, just to see the real pattern. Nobody has time for that, and the results would still be patchy. This is why tracking needs a system, not a habit.


**The Metrics to Track**


Before you set anything up, get clear on what you're measuring. These five metrics give you a full picture of where you stand:


- **Mentions.** How often your brand name appears in AI answers for the prompts you care about. This is your baseline. If you're not mentioned, nothing else matters yet.
- **Citations.** How often the AI links to your website (or content about you) as a source. A mention means the model knows you. A citation means it trusts your content enough to point people to it.
- Visibility Score. A single number that rolls your presence into one figure. The better scores weigh where you appear in each answer, how you're described, and how much competitors dominate the response, and they count answers that don't mention you as zero. It's the metric you'll report to your boss, and the easiest way to spot trends over weeks and months.
- **Sentiment.** Whether the AI talks about you in a positive, neutral or negative way. Being mentioned as "a pricier option with a clunky interface" isn't a win. Sentiment tells you how the model frames you.
- **Share of voice versus competitors.** Your slice of all brand mentions in your category compared to your rivals. If you appear in 30% of answers but your main competitor appears in 70%, you know exactly how big the gap is.


Each metric answers a different question. Mentions and citations tell you if you're present. Visibility Score tells you if you're improving. Sentiment tells you how you're being described. Share of voice tells you whether you're winning or losing ground in your market.Track all five together and you'll rarely be caught off guard.


**How to Track Your AI Visibility, Step by Step**


Here's the setup process from start to finish. You can follow it with any tracking tool, though some make certain steps much easier than others.


**Step 1: Choose the Prompts Your Buyers Actually Ask**


Your tracking is only as good as the prompts you feed it. Pick questions that sound like real buyers, not like your marketing team.


Split them into three groups:


- **Unbranded prompts.** Questions about your category or problem with no brand named. Think "what's the best CRM for a small sales team" or "how do I reduce customer churn." These matter most, because this is where new buyers discover you.
- **Branded prompts.** Questions that include your name, like "is \[your brand\] good for enterprise teams" or "what does \[your brand\] cost." These show you how the AI describes you when someone already knows who you are.
- **Comparison prompts.** Head‑to‑head questions such as "\[your brand\] vs \[competitor\]" or "alternatives to \[competitor\]." Buyers ask these right before they decide, so the stakes are high.


Talk to your sales team. Read support tickets. Look at the questions people type into your site search and the queries in Google Search Console. The language your buyers use is the language you should track. Start with a focused set that covers your core category questions, your brand and your main competitors, then grow from there.


**Step 2: Choose the AI Platforms to Monitor**


Your buyers don't all use the same assistant. Some live in ChatGPT. Others rely on Perplexity for research, Gemini because it's built into their Google account, or Claude for work tasks. And a huge number of people see Google AI Overviews without choosing to, simply because they searched on Google. Start with the platforms your buyers use most. For many brands that means ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Gemini, with Claude and Google AI Mode close behind. If you sell to a specific group, think about where they spend time. Keep in mind that Gemini shows very few source links in its answers, so on Gemini, mentions and Visibility Score tell you more than citation counts.


**Step 3: Run the Prompts on a Daily Schedule, by Market and Language**


Because answers shift from run to run, one check per month won't cut it. Run your prompts every day. Over time, the daily results smooth out the random swings and show you the real trend. If you sell in more than one country, set up separate tracking for each market. Run French prompts for France, German prompts for Germany, and so on. Don't assume your English results carry over. They often don't, and you could be missing a big problem (or a big opportunity) in a market you care about.


**Step 4: Add Your Competitors to Benchmark Against**


Your numbers only make sense next to someone else's. A Visibility Score of 40 could be great in one category and poor in another. Pick three to five direct competitors and track them alongside your own brand. Include the obvious rivals, but also watch for brands that keep appearing in AI answers even if you don't think of them as competition. AI assistants sometimes recommend companies you've never heard of, and those are the ones quietly taking your share of voice.


**Step 5: Analyze Which Sources AI Cites and Why**


This step is where tracking turns into strategy. When an AI assistant recommends a brand, it usually draws from specific sources: review sites, industry blogs, forum threads, YouTube videos, comparison articles and brand websites.


Look at which pages get cited most often for your key prompts. Ask yourself:


- Is your own site being cited, or are third parties telling your story for you?
- Which Reddit threads or YouTube videos keep showing up?
- Do your competitors appear on sites where you're missing?
- What do the most‑cited pages have in common? Are they detailed, recent, well‑structured?


You'll often find that a handful of sources shape most of the answers in your category. Get your brand onto those pages, or create content that's better than them. That's where your effort is most likely to pay off.


**Step 6: Connect Visibility to AI Crawler Activity, Traffic and Conversions**


Visibility is great, but your CFO wants to know if it brings in money. That means tying your AI presence to real outcomes.


Start with AI crawler activity. Bots from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Perplexity visit your site to read your content. Your server logs show which pages they crawl, how often, and whether they hit errors. If a bot can't reach a page, that page can't be cited.


Then track AI‑referred traffic: visitors who land on your site after clicking a link in ChatGPT, Perplexity or another assistant. Follow those visitors through to sign‑ups, demo requests or purchases. Once you can say "AI assistants sent us 1,200 visitors last month and 40 of them became customers," the case for investing in AI visibility makes itself.


**Step 7: Act on the Gaps and Measure Again**


Tracking without action is just watching. Use what you've learned to make changes:


- Write content that answers the prompts where you're missing.
- Update old pages so they're clear, current and easy for AI to quote.
- Get mentioned on the review sites, forums and videos that AI keeps citing.
- Fix technical issues that block AI crawlers.
- Address negative sentiment by correcting outdated information wherever it lives.


Then let your daily tracking show you what worked. Some changes will show up in your numbers within weeks. Others won't move anything, and that's useful to know too. Plan for upkeep as well: Promptwatch's research shows citation relevance holds for roughly 8 to 14 weeks before a content refresh helps. Keep repeating the loop: find the gap, act on it, measure again.

**Start Tracking Before Your Competitors Do**


For more and more buyers, an AI assistant is now where research starts. The brands that show up in those answers today are building a lead that will be hard to close later. You don't need to guess where you stand. Pick your prompts, choose your platforms, track daily, watch your competitors, and act on what the data tells you.


Do that consistently, and AI visibility stops being a mystery. It becomes one more channel you can measure, improve and grow.
